title: AI Usage Event (metadata-only)
description: Canonical schema for AI coding tool usage telemetry. Metadata-only per locked decision: NO prompt/response text, NO file contents, NO code. additionalProperties is false so any attempt to attach content fields fails validation at ingest.

schema_version.description: Schema major.minor version. Additive-only within major v1 (see VERSIONING.md).

event_id.description: Unique event identifier generated by the collector. Used for idempotent ingest/dedup.

ts.description: Event time, RFC 3339, UTC, truncated to SECOND-level precision (no fractional seconds — pattern enforced). Collector clock; ingest records its own receipt timestamp separately.

event_type.description: Event kind. Added in v1.1 ('tool_use'); 'inventory' added in v1.2. OPTIONAL for back-compat — absent means 'usage' (a token-volume/session record). 'tool_use' events carry tool_calls[] (agent tool invocations: shell, file writes, network, MCP calls) instead of token volume. 'inventory' events carry configured_mcp_servers[] (MCP servers present in the tool's config files) and are emitted only when that configuration changes. Metadata-only: names and counts, never arguments, results, commands, or env values.

tool_calls.description: Agent tool-call aggregates for event_type='tool_use' (chain fields / schema v1.10). One entry per (tool, MCP server) per session per flush window — or per discrete call when call_id is present. Metadata-only by the same contract as match_flags: tool name, action class, count, duration, optional chain ids/result status — NEVER arguments, file paths, command lines, or tool output. additionalProperties:false on entries makes any attempt to attach arguments fail ingest validation.

tool_name.description: Tool identifier as the agent framework names it (e.g. 'Bash', 'Edit', 'WebFetch', or the tool part of an MCP name). Fixed vocabulary from the tool's own registry — not user-generated free text.

mcp_server.description: MCP server id when the call went through an MCP server (from the tool's own config name, e.g. 'github' in mcp__github__*). Null for built-in tools. Cleartext by design: it names infrastructure, not user data, and is matched against the approved-server allowlist in policy.

action_class.description: Coarse action classification so policy can reason about agent capabilities without seeing arguments: fs_read (file reads/searches), fs_write (file edits/writes), shell (command execution), network (web fetch/search), mcp_call (any MCP server call), other.

count.description: Number of invocations of this tool in the aggregation window.

duration_ms.description: Total wall time across those invocations when the source can derive it; null otherwise.

call_id.description: Optional opaque call id for MCP/session chain tracing (schema v1.10). Ephemeral, collector-generated or tool-provided random id re-hashed per UTC day with session_id so it cannot profile across days. NEVER contains argument content.

parent_call_id.description: Optional parent call_id when this invocation was nested under another tool call in the same session (schema v1.10). Null when top-level. Enables request→tool→result chain reconstruction without content.

result_status.description: Optional coarse outcome of the tool call (schema v1.10). ok=succeeded, error=tool/runtime failure, denied=endpoint or policy denied the call, unknown=source did not report. NEVER includes error messages, stdout, or result bodies.

seq.description: Optional monotonic sequence within the session flush window (schema v1.10). Used with call_id/parent_call_id to order chain edges when timestamps share second precision.

configured_mcp_servers.description: MCP servers present in the tool's configuration files for event_type='inventory'. Emitted only when the set changes (collector checkpoints a hash of the sorted list). Metadata-only: the server name as the user named it in their own tool config plus the config scope — NEVER command lines, args, URLs, or env values (env may hold secrets). additionalProperties:false on entries makes any attempt to attach config detail fail ingest validation.

name.description: MCP server identifier as configured (e.g. 'github' in mcp__github__*). Cleartext by design: it names infrastructure, not user data, and is matched against the approved-server allowlist in policy.

scope.description: Where the server is configured: 'user' = tool-global/user-level config file, 'project' = a project/workspace-level config file.

host_ref.description: Pseudonymized host/agent id: HMAC-SHA256(hostname, company salt), lowercase hex. Reversible only with the salt, which lives in the platform HSM/KMS, never in collectors.

user_ref.description: Pseudonymized user: HMAC-SHA256(corporate identity, company salt). May be null for proxy-sourced events until identity mapping lands. Identity mapping table is stored separately under stricter access control.

tool.description: First-class tool enum (not the same as the policy allowlist). 'other' = unapproved/unknown tool (detection target, not blocking — observe-only posture v1). 'genai_app' (v1.3) = first-party company application calling an LLM API directly, observed via OTel GenAI instrumentation — NOT an employee coding tool; consumers must exclude it from sanctioned/unapproved tool reporting. 'grok_build' (v1.8) = Grok Build grok_local agent adapter (xAI-backed); first-class so fleet dashboards can name it without collapsing to other — inclusion in approved_tools remains a Security decision.

tool_raw.description: Raw tool identifier as detected (e.g. 'aider', 'copilot'). Populated when tool='other' so unapproved-tool reporting can name the tool. Low-sensitivity metadata; no user-generated content allowed.

tool_version.description: Version of the AI tool binary/plugin. Used for fleet hygiene and vuln exposure views.

model.description: Model identifier (e.g. 'claude-sonnet-4-5'). Null when the source cannot observe it (proxy).

provider.description: LLM provider serving the request (e.g. 'anthropic', 'openai', 'azure-openai', 'aws-bedrock'). Null when unobservable.

session_id.description: Ephemeral session identifier from the tool (random, not user-derived). Correlates events within one working session. Collectors MUST re-hash stable/long-lived tool session ids per UTC day (e.g. HMAC(utc-date || raw_id)) so events cannot be profiled across days.

tokens_in.description: Input/prompt token count for the event. Aggregate volume only — never content.

tokens_out.description: Output/completion token count for the event.

cost_estimate_usd.description: Estimated USD cost computed from token counts and a versioned price table held by the platform (not per-employee billing; capacity/spend visibility).

service_name.description: Application/service identity for source='otel' events (v1.3): the OpenTelemetry resource attribute service.name of the instrumented app. Cleartext by design: it names company infrastructure (same class as mcp_server), never user data. Required when source='otel'.

duration_ms.description: Wall time of the LLM call in milliseconds (v1.3). Latency signal for per-app operational views; derived from OTel span start/end. Optional — endpoint/proxy sources may omit it.

status.description: Outcome of the LLM call (v1.3), from the OTel span status. 'error' = the call failed (provider error, timeout); carries NO error message or body — those are content and are dropped at the receiver.

traffic_class.description: Source-class attribution of the event's origin (v1.4): 'application' = server/DC subnet or CI runner (company-built software), 'employee' = endpoint subnet, 'unknown' = no subnet-inventory match. Classified at the collector from src_ip BEFORE pseudonymization — only the label crosses the wire, never the IP. Proxy events only; absent on endpoint/otel events.

bytes_up.description: Request bytes toward the destination (v1.4). Network volume metadata, not content. Null when the source cannot observe it (Squid access.log carries reply size only).

bytes_down.description: Response bytes from the destination (v1.4). Volume/cost-proxy metering for provider-API traffic. Network volume metadata, not content.

http_status.description: HTTP status code of the transaction when the network source reports it (v1.4). Drives the status-mix view for provider-API traffic; complements 'status' (ok|error) which carries the OTel span outcome.

repo_ref.description: Pseudonymized repository: salted HMAC-SHA256(normalized repo URL) using the same KMS-held salt family as user_ref. NOT a plain hash — repo names are enumerable, so an unsalted hash would be trivially inverted. Note: repo_ref remains INTERNAL-IDENTIFIABLE — anyone holding the salt (platform KMS) can enumerate known repo URLs and match them; it is not linkable outside the platform. Null when no repo context. Never stores repo name, org, or path in the clear.

match_flags.description: Detector results. REQUIRED so 'no flags' is an explicit statement (detectors ran, nothing fired), not missing data. Presence of an entry means the detector fired; the matched content is NEVER stored — only detector name, category, severity, and (v1.8, for secret/pii detectors) a redacted per-occurrence fingerprint plus match location metadata.

category.description: Detection category. 'injection' is an additive enum extension: prompt-injection / jailbreak phrasing detectors.

severity.description: Alert routing hint. Optional; policy engine may re-derive.

fingerprint.description: Redacted per-occurrence fingerprint (v1.8), present only for secret/pii detectors: truncated (64-bit) HMAC-SHA256 of the NFKC-folded, whitespace-stripped MATCHED TEXT, keyed with the company KMS salt and domain-separated ('fp1') from the pseudonym HMACs so it cannot be cross-correlated with host_ref/user_ref/repo_ref of the same string. Proves a specific secret instance fired and dedupes repeat sightings of the same secret across events and sessions — WITHOUT storing the secret. NOT reversible: verifying a match requires authorized endpoint access plus the KMS salt (re-hash the suspected value and compare). Stable only while the salt is unchanged (same caveat as repo_ref); salt rotation restarts dedupe continuity. Never a plain/unsalted hash — low-entropy PII (emails, national ids) would be dictionary-invertible.

offset.description: Character offset of the match within the scanned surface (v1.8). Position metadata only — helps an authorized analyst locate the match when re-running the detector on the endpoint; carries no content. Present iff fingerprint is.

surface.description: Which matcher scan pass produced the match (v1.8): 'raw' = original text, 'normalized' = NFKC/confusable-folded, 'squashed' = whitespace-deleted, 'base64' = inside a decoded base64 blob. Tells the verifying analyst which surface 'offset' refers to. Present iff fingerprint is.

enforcement.description: Endpoint inline-enforcement audit record (v1.5 amended 2026-07-22 to 'observe + endpoint blocking for critical rules', approved). Present only on events where an endpoint hook computed an enforcement decision: 'blocked' = the prompt/tool call was actually denied; 'would_block' = shadow mode, the decision was computed and logged but NOT applied; 'confirmed' (v1.6) = a confirm/break-glass rule challenged the first submission and the user explicitly overrode by resubmitting the identical prompt within the challenge window — the content was allowed through. Used by pii-in-prompt (confirm) and secret-pattern-in-prompt (break-glass override). 'redacted' (v1.10) = the secret-in-tool-input rule rewrote the matched secret spans in a PreToolUse tool_input to [REDACTED:<detector>] markers and the tool call PROCEEDED with the redacted input — the secret never left the endpoint. Metadata-only by the same contract as match_flags: rule id + action + policy hash — never the matched content, the blocked payload, the redacted/original input, or the user-visible reason string.

action.description: 'blocked' = enforcement applied (prompt blocked / tool call denied). 'would_block' = shadow mode: the rule would have fired, nothing was interrupted. The shadow/enforce distinction is what makes the pre-rollout bake measurable. 'confirmed' (v1.6) = user resubmitted identical prompt to confirm (PII) or break-glass override a secret block; the prompt proceeded. Confirms/overrides are the audit trail for intentional sends. 'redacted' (v1.10) = the tool call proceeded after the endpoint rewrote matched secret spans to [REDACTED:<detector>] markers; redactions are the audit trail for secrets stopped without stopping the work.

rule_id.description: Endpoint-enforceable rule that fired (e.g. 'secret-pattern-in-prompt', 'unapproved-mcp-server'). Fixed vocabulary from the collector's enforcement ruleset — not user-generated text.

policy_hash.description: Hash/version tag of the endpoint enforcement policy bundle the decision was computed from (audit continuity, same role as policy_hash in the guardrail engine). Optional; omitted when the deployment does not version its bundle.

cohort_member.description: Whether this endpoint is inside the active enforce canary cohort for the loaded bundle (v1.11). Present only when the policy engine exposes cohort membership.

decision_latency_ms.description: Wall-clock milliseconds spent on the endpoint enforcement decision path for this hook invocation (v1.10). Measured around local rule evaluation only — never includes network I/O to the control plane.

rails.description: Multi-rail attribution when two or more rails fired (schema v1.11). First entry matches primary action/rule_id.

enforcement_posture.description: Endpoint enforcement COVERAGE marker (v1.7). Emitted by every enforcement-aware endpoint hook on every event it produces, whether or not a rule fired — this is the denominator that makes `enforcement` counts readable. Without it, zero `enforcement` records is ambiguous between three very different states: the endpoint runs a earlier collector, the endpoint runs a current collector but no policy bundle was ever delivered to it, or the endpoint is genuinely clean. Only the last one is a safe basis for flipping a rule to enforce, so the shadow-bake report treats a missing denominator as NO COVERAGE rather than as a clean result. Pure posture metadata: no content, no counts of user activity beyond the event that carries it.

policy.description: 'loaded' = an enforcement policy bundle was found and parsed on this endpoint, so rules can fire. 'absent' = no bundle (or an unreadable/malformed one, which fails open to the same behaviour): this endpoint can NEVER produce an enforcement record, and counting it as clean is the bug this field exists to prevent.

mode.description: The bundle's global mode — the fleet-wide kill switch. Present only when policy='loaded'. 'shadow' = decisions are computed and audited but never applied.

evaluated.description: True when this specific hook invocation actually ran the enforcement rules over its payload (UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse). False for events from hooks that carry no enforceable surface (SessionStart/SessionEnd/PostToolUse) — they still prove the endpoint's posture, but they are not prompts, so the bake's per-prompt denominator counts only evaluated=true.

policy_hash.description: Hash/version tag of the loaded bundle, so coverage can be attributed to a specific ruleset revision (same role as enforcement.policy_hash). Optional; omitted when the deployment does not version its bundle.

enforcement_latency_ms.description: Wall-clock ms for local enforcement decision path (v1.10).

cohort_member.description: Whether endpoint is in active enforce canary cohort (v1.11).

then.description: An endpoint with no bundle has no kill-switch state and no ruleset revision to report. Rejecting the combination keeps an unenforceable endpoint from being counted as covered capacity in the bake denominator.

source.description: Collection point. 'endpoint' = tool hook collector on the device (depth); 'proxy' = network/proxy log ingestion (breadth); 'otel' (v1.3) = OTLP receiver accepting OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic-convention spans from instrumented first-party applications (APM-class service telemetry, not employee monitoring); 'os_egress' (v1.9) = on-device OS egress / DNS / flow metadata for AI SaaS domains (browser and desktop clients) — hostname-level presence only, no URL paths or bodies. Determines which fields can be null.

agent_handoffs.description: A2A / multi-agent handoff visibility (schema v1.10). Emitted when a coding tool spawns a sub-agent, Task tool, or peer agent. Metadata only: session linkage + kind + status — NEVER prompts, plans, or tool results from the child agent. additionalProperties:false on entries.

handoff_kind.description: How the parent agent spawned work: subagent (nested agent loop), task (Task/Todo tool style), delegate (peer handoff), other.

status.description: Handoff lifecycle status. Outcome only — no failure reason text.

child_session_id.description: Ephemeral child session id (same daily re-hash rule as session_id). Null when the tool did not expose a child session.

tool_name.description: Parent tool that initiated the handoff when known (e.g. Task, Agent). Fixed vocabulary / framework name — not free text.

parent_call_id.description: Optional link to tool_calls[].call_id that spawned this handoff.

then.description: Endpoint collectors observe tool internals; model and token counts should normally be present.
OTel app-telemetry events must carry the application's service.name — per-app attribution is the entire point of this source.
tool_use events must carry their tool-call aggregates; a tool_use event without tool_calls is a collector bug.
inventory events must carry the configured MCP server list (possibly empty — an explicit 'no servers configured' statement); an inventory event without configured_mcp_servers is a collector bug.
